title: Skeleton Coding: Program Structure as a Specification for Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.38214v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Coding agents are typically provided end-to-end behavioral specifications that the code they produce should satisfy, such as tests and input--output examples. How many such specifications must a developer provide, and which ones, for the agent to produce the developer's intended program? We argue that this cannot be determined a priori, for it depends on the structure of the implementation, which is left to the agent to decide. An agent first commits to a structure---a decomposition into data types, modules, and functions---which fixes a class of candidate programs; behavioral specifications then select a program within that class. A set of tests that suffices for one structure may leave another badly underdetermined, requiring different edge cases or exponentially more examples. translated_title: 骨架编码：将程序结构作为智能体的规约
translated_abstract: 编码智能体通常会被提供端到端的行为规约，即其生成的代码应满足的条件，例如测试用例和输入-输出示例。开发者需要提供多少这样的规约，以及提供哪些规约，才能让智能体生成开发者所期望的程序？我们认为这个问题无法先验确定，因为它取决于实现的结构，而结构是由智能体自行决定的。智能体首先会确定一个结构——即分解为数据类型、模块和函数的方式——这固定了一类候选程序；行为规约随后在该类程序中选出一个程序。对某种结构而言足够的测试集，对另一种结构可能严重欠定，需要不同的边界用例或指数级更多的示例。由于结构由智能体选择，开发者若不从数千行代码中逆向工程，就无法确保其规约是完备的（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 论文提出“骨架编码”概念，指出智能体在行为规约选定程序之前会先确定程序结构，而测试等规约是否充分取决于该结构本身，因此开发者应将程序结构（数据类型、模块与函数的分解）作为一种规约提供给智能体。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "Skeleton Coding," arguing that since an agent commits to a program structure before behavioral specifications select a program within that class, the sufficiency of specifications like tests depends on that structure—so developers should treat the program structure itself as a specification for coding agents.
